candidate.title: Drop-ChIP
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina Drop-ChIP schematic, interpreted as the native-chromatin droplet indexing and pooled-ChIP architecture described by Rotem et al. (2015). The continuous material route starts at 'Cell suspension'; the far-left 'Single cell'/nucleosome vignette introduces the assay and chromatin target. The upper 'Droplet with unique oligos' input converges at fusion; no alternative target workflow or retained output split is depicted. The matching collection page uses 'Drop-ChIP or scChIP-seq' as local naming for this schematic, not as evidence that all single-cell ChIP-seq implementations share it. Demulsification/carrier addition and one broad library-preparation interface are explicit source-supported interpretations of the PNG's compressed route. The schematic leaves the antibody epitope generic; the paper demonstrates separate H3K4me3 and H3K4me2 assays. This extraction does not add the paper's unpictured downstream clustering or reconstruct a laboratory recipe.

operations.label: Load single cells into droplets with lysis buffer and MNase
operations.description: Encapsulate individual cells with lysis/digestion reagents. Cell lysis releases chromatin, and MNase fragmentation produces nucleosome-associated DNA retained within each originating droplet.
operations.mechanism: Lysis reagent disrupts cells; MNase preferentially cuts accessible linker DNA in the reported implementation. These are reagent/enzyme functions within the loading block, not additional sequenced materials.
operations.information_effect: Establishes physical cell-level partitioning before chromatin from different cells can be mixed.

operations.label: Fuse droplets
operations.description: Merge a single-cell chromatin droplet with a barcode-adaptor droplet. The paper resolves the downstream tagging transformation: adaptors are ligated to nucleosomal DNA ends within the fused compartment.
operations.mechanism: The reported three-point merger uses electric-field-triggered coalescence and introduces enzymatic labeling buffer containing DNA ligase. The buffer supports end repair and blunt-end ligation; ligase is a reagent, not the readout carrier.
operations.information_effect: Converts spatial provenance into a covalent cell-index/genomic-DNA association that survives later release and bulk ChIP. The intended informative product carries matching cell indexes on both ends; alternative loading/fusion outcomes limit certainty.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and figure identify Drop-ChIP alone. All five named transformations in the drawn main route apply to it: loading/lysis/MNase digestion, fusion/tagging, droplet pooling, ChIP and sequencing. The separately represented release/carrier and broad library operations explain required material interfaces reported by the cited implementation and catalogue; they are not additional assay targets. The oligo droplet is an input branch, and MNase, ligase and antibody are local reagents/components. The left vignette is an assay/analyte illustration, with no connector into the cell-suspension workflow. The inspected collection-page heading and its identical figure establish a matching secondary source; its scChIP-seq wording is a local alias in this context.
